# Workflows API

Manage workflow records, inspect runs, and trigger execution. The create example saves a disabled draft; configure a valid system_spec before enabling a workflow.

Use [API authentication](authentication.md) for protected requests. Examples use your own resource IDs and a temporary token; saved response examples are synthetic.

| Method | Path | Operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/workflow` | [List workflows](#op-get-v1-workflow) |
| `POST` | `/v1/workflow` | [Create workflow](#op-post-v1-workflow) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workflow/{id}` | [Get workflow](#op-get-v1-workflow-id) |
| `PUT` | `/v1/workflow/{id}` | [Update workflow](#op-put-v1-workflow-id) |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/workflow/{id}` | [Delete workflow](#op-delete-v1-workflow-id) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workflow/{id}/runs` | [List workflow runs](#op-get-v1-workflow-id-runs) |
| `POST` | `/v1/workflow/{id}/runs` | [Run workflow](#op-post-v1-workflow-id-runs) |
| `GET` | `/v1/workflow/{id}/logs` | [Get workflow logs](#op-get-v1-workflow-id-logs) |

## List workflows {#op-get-v1-workflow}

`GET /v1/workflow`

Returns a paginated list of Workflow

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |
| `page` | query | no | Page number |
| `per_page` | query | no | Items per page |

### Request example

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --request GET "$ADIOS_API_URL/v1/workflow" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: $ADIOS_TEAM_ID"
```


### Response: HTTP 200

List of Workflow

### Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | array |  |
| `data[].created_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].data` | object | Workflow designer state and API-facing metadata |
| `data[].deleted_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].enabled` | boolean |  |
| `data[].owner_id` | string |  |
| `data[].region` | string |  |
| `data[].status` | string |  Allowed: draft, active, disabled, archived, deleted. |
| `data[].system_spec` | object | Canonical system workflow specification synced to the system backend |
| `data[].team_id` | string |  |
| `data[].title` | string |  |
| `data[].updated_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].workflow_id` | string |  |
| `pagination` | object |  |
| `pagination.page` | integer | Current page number |
| `pagination.per_page` | integer | Number of items per page |
| `pagination.total` | integer | Total number of items |

Illustrative example; not a live response:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "created_at": 1791072000,
      "data": {},
      "deleted_at": 0,
      "enabled": true,
      "owner_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
      "region": "",
      "status": "draft",
      "system_spec": {},
      "team_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
      "title": "Postman example",
      "updated_at": 1791072000,
      "workflow_id": "000000000000000000000000001"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 1,
    "total": 1
  }
}
```


## Create workflow {#op-post-v1-workflow}

`POST /v1/workflow`

Creates a new Workflow

This request changes data or starts an action. Review the target and body before sending it.

Request fields (the body contains an editable example):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | object | no | Workflow designer state and API-facing metadata |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes |  Default: `true`. |
| `owner_id` | string | no |  |
| `region` | string | no |  Default: `""`. |
| `status` | string | yes |  Allowed: draft, active, disabled, archived, deleted. Default: `"draft"`. |
| `system_spec` | object | no | Canonical system workflow specification synced to the system backend |
| `team_id` | string | yes |  |
| `title` | string | yes |  |

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |

### Request example

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --request POST "$ADIOS_API_URL/v1/workflow" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: $ADIOS_TEAM_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
  "team_id": "YOUR_TEAM_ID",
  "title": "Postman example workflow",
  "status": "draft",
  "enabled": false
}
JSON
```

Replace `YOUR_*` body placeholders before sending. The quoted heredoc keeps the JSON literal.

### Response: HTTP 201

Workflow created

### Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `created_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data` | object | Workflow designer state and API-facing metadata |
| `deleted_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `enabled` | boolean |  |
| `owner_id` | string |  |
| `region` | string |  |
| `status` | string |  Allowed: draft, active, disabled, archived, deleted. |
| `system_spec` | object | Canonical system workflow specification synced to the system backend |
| `team_id` | string |  |
| `title` | string |  |
| `updated_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `workflow_id` | string |  |

Illustrative example; not a live response:

```json
{
  "created_at": 1791072000,
  "data": {},
  "deleted_at": 0,
  "enabled": true,
  "owner_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
  "region": "",
  "status": "draft",
  "system_spec": {},
  "team_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
  "title": "Postman example",
```

## Run workflow {#op-post-v1-workflow-id-runs}

`POST /v1/workflow/{id}/runs`

Set `workflow_id` using IDs from your own API responses.
